about: The `annual_report_catalogue` table, published whole. See /api/schema for its grain. This file is fy 2021 only.

provenance.warning: These figures cite a document not present in the document table, so no address can be given for them. Treat any figure resting on them as uncheckable.

rows.name: Table of contents
rows.what_it_is: The report's own index with printed folio numbers, or 'No Report Submitted' where a committee filed nothing.
rows.layout: Two columns grouped under ADMINISTRATION / TOWN SERVICES / PROTECTION OF PERSONS & PROPERTY / PLANNING / EDUCATION / TOWN CLERK / MISCELLANEOUS INFORMATION.
rows.notes: This is where the financial schedules get their names: 'Balance Sheet for year ending June 30, 2021' (22), 'General Funds Revenue Chart' (23), 'FY 2021 Receipts' (24), 'General Fund Expenditures Chart' (25), 'General Fund Appropriations Summary & Classification of Accounts' (26), 'Special Revenue Funds' (31), 'Capital Projects Fund' (36), 'Treasurer's Cash as of June 30, 2021' (38), 'Trust Funds' (39), 'Five Year Outstanding Debt' (41), 'Debt Repayment Schedule' (42), 'Collection of Taxes' (46). NOTE: the contents page lists a 'Vital Records Report' at folio 137, but folio 137 (PDF p138) carries the Annual Town Meeting record and NO vital records report appears anywhere in the document -- unlike FY2019, which prints one. Four committees filed 'No Report Submitted': Agricultural Commission, Housing Authority, Information Technology, and one other.

rows.name: Town facts panel
rows.printed_heading: ANNUAL TOWN ELECTION- 3RD SATURDAY IN MAY / ANNUAL TOWN MEETING- 1ST SATURDAY IN MAY / AREA-26.63 SQUARE MILES / ROAD MILES-ABOUT 100
rows.what_it_is: Standing facts about the town printed above the descriptive narrative.
rows.layout: Centred label lines above narrative paragraphs.
rows.notes: Unlike FY2019, this panel does NOT print the tax rate. The FY2021 rate has to be taken from the assessors' page (p38), which prints 17.19 in the table and 17.74 in the prose -- see that entry. The paragraph below the panel says 'Select Board' where FY2019 said 'Board of Selectmen', and mentions the Agricultural Commission (2013) and Architectural Preservation District (2015) bylaws that FY2019's version does not.

rows.name: Federal and state legislator directory
rows.printed_heading: MASSACHUSETTS CONGRESSIONAL DELEGATION / SENATE / STATE LEGISLATORS
rows.what_it_is: Contact details for the two US Senators, the US Representative, the State Senator and the two State Representatives covering Lunenburg.
rows.columns: name and office | address | telephone | email
rows.layout: Address blocks, two facing columns for the Senate.
rows.notes: The state delegation changed completely between FY2019 and FY2021: Senator Dean A. Tran replaced by John Cronin, Rep. Jennifer E. Benson by Danillo Sena, Rep. Stephan Hay by Michael Kushmerek. Unlike FY2019 this listing does NOT record which precincts each House member covers.

rows.name: Elected officials and term-expiry years
rows.printed_heading: (board headings printed, e.g. 'Select Board - (5 members) 3 year term')
rows.what_it_is: Every elected office with its incumbents, member count, term length and the year each term expires.
rows.columns: board / office (with member count and term length) | name | term expiry year
rows.layout: Centred single column grouped by board; the opening board (Board of Assessors or Board of Health) lost its heading with the top of p8.
rows.notes: Records vacancies and mid-term departures explicitly: Housing Authority '1 Vacancy' and 'Governor Appointee-vacant'; Trust Fund Commission '1 Vacancy-failure to elect'; Sewer Commission 'Carl Luck-resigned 4/30/2021'. School Committee is described as '(5 members)' here while the FY2019 report's town profile says the committee has seven members -- worth checking against the bylaw before quoting either.

rows.name: Appointed officials, boards and committees
rows.printed_heading: (committee names in caps, e.g. 'HISTORICAL COMMISSION- 3 year term (not less than 3 nor more than 7 members)')
rows.what_it_is: Every appointed committee, board and town officer with members, the seat each represents, and term-expiry years.
rows.columns: committee / office | name | representing | term expiry year
rows.layout: Centred single column, alphabetical by committee, across seven pages.
rows.notes: Includes single-officer appointments (Hazardous Waste Coordinator, Hearings Officer, Pound Keeper, Tree Warden, Town Clockwinders) alongside multi-member committees. Some committees carry their statutory size in the heading. Compare with the FY2019 list to see the turnover: Police Chief is Thomas Gammel here, James Marino in FY2019 (and Marino appears on the FY2021 Select Board).

rows.name: Combined balance sheet, all fund types, 30 June 2021
rows.printed_heading: (the title and column headings are on the lost top band; the contents page calls it 'Balance Sheet for year ending June 30, 2021')
rows.what_it_is: The town-wide balance sheet: receivables by levy year, betterments, tax liens, due-to/due-from, then liabilities and fund equity, across six fund columns.
rows.grain: one balance-sheet line item across six fund columns
rows.columns: line item | GENERAL FUND | SPECIAL REVENUE | ENTERPRISE | CAPITAL PROJECT | TRUST and AGENCY | GENERAL LONG-TERM DEBT
rows.layout: Seven columns, rows in proper order. Column headings and the opening cash/receivable rows were lost with the page's top band; the first surviving row is 'FY16 REAL ESTATE TAXES'.
rows.notes: Cleaner than the FY2019 equivalent and it fully reconciles: liabilities plus fund equity equal total assets in every column, which the FY2019 sheet did not do in the Trust and Agency column. Long-term debt $41,885,307 ties to the five-year debt table on p42. RESERVED FOR ENCUMBRANCES $316,972.56 ties exactly to the encumbered column of the appropriations GRAND TOTAL on p31. General fund undesignated fund balance is $3,045,442.99, roughly double the FY2019 figure of $1,463,528.53 -- the free-cash effect of the COVID year. Two new rows appear that FY2019 does not have: RESERVED FOR ENDOWMENTS $668,915.17 and DUE FROM COMMONWEALTH OF MASS.

rows.name: General fund revenues pie chart, FY2021
rows.printed_heading: GENERAL FUND REVENUES FY 21
rows.what_it_is: A pie chart of general fund revenue by source with percentage labels.
rows.columns: source | percent of general fund revenues
rows.layout: Pie chart; only the slice labels and percentages OCR.
rows.notes: PROPERTY [TAXES] 65.5[%], STATE-LOCAL AID 22.48%, ALL OTHER 7.45%, MOTOR VEHICLE EXCISE 4.47%. Those sum to 99.9%. Worth noting against FY2019: that report's revenue chart is MISSING -- its p29 and p31 both carry the expenditure chart -- so this is the earlier of the two years for which a revenue split is actually published.

rows.name: FY 2021 receipts, by revenue source
rows.printed_heading: FY 2021 RECEIPTS - JUNE 2021
rows.what_it_is: Every general fund revenue line collected in FY2021, grouped as TAXES & EXCISES, INTEREST, DEMANDS, FEES, DEPARTMENTAL REVENUE, LICENSES/PERMITS, STATE REVENUE, FINES & FORFEITS, INVESTMENT INCOME, TRANSFERS and NON RECURRING REVENUE, then re-totalled in a SUMMARY OF RECEIPTS block.

rows.printed_total: A 'GRAND TOTAL' row is printed at the foot of the SUMMARY OF RECEIPTS block, but its value falls in the clipped third column and is NOT recoverable from this text.
rows.notes: SAME LIMITATION AS FY2019: the rendering hard-clips at 188 characters and every AMOUNT in the third column is cut off, though the labels survive. Lost that way: NET METERING CREDITS, SCHOOL BASED MEDICARE, LOCK UP FEES, BID CHARGES, FEDERAL REVENUE, PREMIUM SALE OF BONDS, SALE OF TOWN EQUIPMENT, MISC. REVENUE, MEDICAL RECORDS, EARNINGS ON INVESTMENTS, INVESTMENT INCOME, PRIOR YEAR EXCISE, PRIOR YEAR INT/DEMAND, TRANSFERS FROM OTHER FUNDS, NON RECURRING REVENUE and the whole SUMMARY OF RECEIPTS with its GRAND TOTAL. FEDERAL REVENUE is the one that matters most in a COVID year and it is exactly the one clipped. Recoverable in full: REAL ESTATE TAXES $27,884,944.92, CH 70 SCHOOL AID $7,773,938.00, MOTOR VEHICLE EXCISE $1,978,654.29, UNRESTRICTED GEN'L GOVT AID $1,122,928.00, MSBA REIMB-SCHOOL $474,239.00, RESCUE WAGON $254,262.15, BUILDING PERMITS $244,736.50, ZONING INCENTIVE $210,000.00 (new since FY2019), LOCAL OPTION MEALS TAX $125,662.18, SMART GROWTH 40S $79,717.00, ROOM OCCUPANCY EXCISE $104.47 (a COVID-year collapse), COURT FINES $12,912.60 (against $20,083.41 in FY2019), DOG FINES $50.00 (against $6,755.00).

rows.name: General fund appropriations summary and classification of accounts, FY2021
rows.printed_heading: (the title band did not OCR; the contents page calls it 'General Fund Appropriations Summary & Classification of Accounts')
rows.what_it_is: The core spending schedule: every FY2021 general fund appropriation line split into payroll and other-expenses sub-lines with department subtotals, showing appropriated, carried forward, available, expended, encumbered and returned to revenue. Runs from Selectmen's Administration through Schools, Insurance, Debt and Interest, State & County Assessments and Transfers to Other Funds.
rows.grain: one appropriation sub-line or department subtotal row
rows.columns: PROGRAM NAME | APPROPRIATED (with fwd/srt/rft carry-forward on its own line) | TOTAL FUNDS AVAILABLE | TOTAL EXPENDED | TOTAL ENCUMBERED | BALANCE TO REVENUE
rows.layout: Six columns over five pages; department name on its own line with indented sub-lines and an unlabelled subtotal after each. Column headings lost with the top band of p27.
rows.printed_total: GRAND TOTAL $44,155,534.50 | $44,155,534.50 | $42,460,920.04 | $316,972.56 | $1,377,641.90 (PDF p31 line 42), followed by the reconciliation legend 'fwd - forward from FY 2020 $838,486.09 / srt - Salary Reserve Transfer $1,297.60 / rft - Reserve Fund Transfer $0.00'.
rows.notes: THE BIGGEST RECOVERY IN THIS DOCUMENT, and cleaner than the FY2019 equivalent -- both the appropriated and available columns of the GRAND TOTAL agree, which they did not in FY2019. Named subtotals: Police Department $1,852,964.66 appropriated / $1,789,174.00 spent; Fire Department $1,183,905.95 / $1,179,678.06; School Department $21,123,602.00 / $20,527,920.43; Monty Tech Assessment $888,684.00 / $876,598.00; Total Insurance $2,633,155.17 / $2,382,566.91; County Retirement Assessment $1,502,144.00; Principal Serial Loans $3,226,042.07; Interest Serial Loans $1,460,268.79; Transfer to Capital Project Fund $1,226,387.39. The State & County Assessments block overspent again, $1,036,576.00 appropriated against $1,095,560.00 spent, driven by Charter Tuitions ($398,681 against $452,612) -- and Charter Tuitions has risen 49% from FY2019's $267,080. The Reserve Fund's whole $75,000 went unspent. The encumbered column ties to RESERVED FOR ENCUMBRANCES on the balance sheet. A COVID note worth reading against rule 11: Fire Payroll-Firefighters/Daymen was appropriated $742,620.05 and spent $881,984.63 while Payroll-E.M.S. was appropriated $158,239.60 and spent $58,164.31 -- the department total still came in under budget, so the movement is between sub-lines, not a cost increase.

rows.name: Special revenue funds, year ending 30 June 2021
rows.printed_heading: (title band lost; contents page calls it 'Special Revenue Funds')
rows.what_it_is: Every fund outside the general fund: revolving funds, state and federal grants including the COVID relief programmes, gift funds, receipts reserved, and the Water, Sewer, Solid Waste and PEG Access enterprise funds. Grouped by GENERAL GOVERNMENT, SCHOOL DEPARTMENT, PUBLIC SAFETY, PARKS & RECREATION, HIGHWAY DEPARTMENT, COUNCIL ON AGING, LIBRARY, CEMETERIES and UNCLASSIFIED.
rows.columns: fund name | balance forward 7/1/2020 | receipts | disbursements | balance forward 7/1/2021
rows.layout: Five columns over five pages with caps section headings. The first page's headings and opening rows were lost with the top band.
rows.notes: THE SINGLE MOST USEFUL COVID TABLE IN EITHER REPORT, and it is now fully readable row by row. Federal and state relief money, each with its own line: ARPA Funds $0.00 forward / $614,195.58 received / nothing spent / $614,195.58 carried (matched on p39 by 'Unibank ARPA CLFRF Fund $614,195.58'); FEMA #4496 - COVID Grant (-$34,094.82) forward / $40,816.99 spent / (-$74,911.81) carried -- i.e. the town was $74,911.81 ahead of reimbursement at year end; FY21 School Reopening #102 $377,550.00 received and $377,528.37 spent; FY21 ESSER #113 $197,973.00 / $197,886.50; Covid Prevention Grant $67,075.00 / $67,075.00; Remote Learning Tech #117/118 $55,735.00 / $55,735.00; Center for Tech & Civic Life Grant $5,000.00 (the private election-administration grant). Other notable rows: Sewer Enterprise Fund $1,398,822.65 / $1,269,129.95 / $1,042,471.79 / $1,625,480.81; PEG Access Enterprise Fund $750,237.94 / $200,083.14 / $92,823.26 / $857,497.82 (ties to the PEG statement on p73); Solid Waste/Recycling Enterprise Fund $10,389.82 / $434,168.42 / $310,962.35 / $133,595.89; Artificial Turf Revolving $51,569.44 / $45,000.00 / $46,473.00. Several funds close negative because spending ran ahead of reimbursement: North Cemetery Accessibility Grant (-$32,000.00), Primary School Alarm System Earmark (-$25,000.00), Mass Trails Grant (-$3,734.85), Firefighter Turnout Gear Grant (-$2,057.82).

rows.name: Capital projects fund, FY2021
rows.printed_heading: (title band lost; contents page calls it 'Capital Projects Fund')
rows.what_it_is: Every open capital authorisation tied to the town meeting article that voted it, with amount carried forward or newly appropriated, amount expended, and balance still open.
rows.columns: article # and meeting (e.g. '6 6/20 ATM') | project and department | appropriated / forward | expended | balance
rows.layout: Five columns; article/meeting references on group heading rows with projects indented beneath, legend at the foot.
rows.printed_total: Grand Total $7,458,008.31 | $6,599,926.64 | $858,081.67, followed by 'fwd - forward from FY 20 / ATM - Annual Town Meeting / STM - Special Town Meeting'
rows.notes: Fully legible. Note the FY2021 Annual Town Meeting was held on 13 June 2020, not in May -- the article references read '6 6/20 ATM', a COVID-displaced meeting date. The FY21 Capital Program block is the year's new spending: Police Vehicle 2 Marked New $134,000.00; SCBA Complement Replacement (1/2) - Fire $115,000.00; Carport Reconfiguration - Public Safety Building $135,000.00 (entirely unspent); Carpet - Lunenburg Public Library $126,000.00 ($53,035.00 spent); Flat Hill Culvert Design $112,500.00; Acquisition of Streetlights $91,000.00 (unspent, voted at the 11/20 Special Town Meeting); Town Hall ADA Ramp/Sidewalk $22,000.00 (unspent). Compared with FY2019 the fund has shrunk sharply -- the school construction and pavement management authorisations that dominated it have closed out. One value carries an OCR space: '$26, 138.82'.

rows.name: Fiscal 2021 assessments and revenues by major class
rows.printed_heading: Town of Lunenburg -Board of Assessors / Fiscal 2021 Assessments and Revenues by Major Class
rows.what_it_is: The tax classification table: each property class with its share of the levy, valuation, tax rate and the levy raised.
rows.columns: Property Class | Levy Percent | Valuations by Class | Tax Rate | Tax Levy
rows.layout: Five columns, four class rows plus Totals, at the foot of the Assessors' narrative page.
rows.notes: READ THE TOTALS ROW WITH CARE -- IT DOES NOT TIE TO ITS OWN COLUMNS. Rows: Residential 91.0772 / 1,587,173,648.00 / 17.19 / 27,283,515.01; Commercial 4.3140 / 75,178,002.00 / 17.19 / 1,292,309.85; Industrial 1.4121 / 24,608,600.00 / 17.19 / 423,021.83; Personal Property 3.1967 / 55,708,508.00 / 17.19 / 957,630.49. The four valuations sum to 1,742,668,758 against a printed Totals of 1,548,256,450, and the four levies sum to 29,956,477.18 against a printed Totals of 28,054,406.88. The class shares are internally consistent with the COLUMN sum (residential is 91.08% of 1,742,668,758) and each class's levy equals its valuation times 17.19/1000, so the four class rows are self-consistent and the Totals row is the odd one out. SEPARATELY, the narrative on the same page says 'The tax rate went from $18.12 to $17.74 for FY 2021' while the table says 17.19. The report contradicts itself on the FY2021 tax rate; do not quote either figure without the PDF. FY2019's equivalent table gave 18.68.

rows.name: Treasurer's cash as of 30 June 2021
rows.printed_heading: (title band lost; contents page calls it "Treasurer's Cash as of June 30, 2021")
rows.what_it_is: Every bank account and investment the Treasurer held at year end, named by institution and purpose, with the balance in each.
rows.layout: Two columns, one row per account, ending with petty cash and a total.
rows.notes: Cash rose $5.4m from FY2019's $15,084,021.00. New named accounts since FY2019: 'Unibank ARPA CLFRF Fund $614,195.58' (the Coronavirus Local Fiscal Recovery Funds, matching the ARPA line in the special revenue funds table) and 'Main Street Bank-PEG Access Enterprise $865,720.18'. Purpose-named earmarks: Main Street Bank-Sewer Enterprise $1,486,584.81; Main Street Bank-Vehicle/Equipment Stabilization $1,201,170.65 (nearly double FY2019); TD BankNorth Zoning Stabilization $230,748.05; Unibank Sewer Reserve Capacity Stabilization $68,198.42; Unibank State Depository $2,893,196.44. Absent since FY2019: Belmont Savings Bank, an 'OPEB' cash line, and the Fidelity ARRA/Senior grant accounts persist at a few dollars.

rows.name: Trust and OPEB funds, FY2021
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG / TRUST AND OPEB FUNDS
rows.what_it_is: Every trust, scholarship and stabilization fund with beginning market value, beginning principal, beginning earnings, net earnings, transfers of principal and earnings, ending cash value and the change in unrealised gain or loss.
rows.grain: one named trust or stabilization fund
rows.columns: ACCOUNT NUMBER | FUND NAME | FY 2021 BEGINNING MARKET VALUE | FY 2021 BEGINNING PRINCIPAL | FY 2021 BEGINNING EARNINGS | FY 2021 NET EARNINGS | FY 2021 TRANSFERS OF PRINCIPAL | FY 2021 TRANSFERS OF EARNINGS | FY 2021 ENDING CASH VALUE | FY 2021 CHANGE IN UNREALIZED GAIN/LOSS | FY 2021 ENDING MARKET VALUE
rows.layout: Eleven columns grouped under CEMETERY FUNDS, CONSERVATION FUNDS, LIBRARY FUNDS, SCHOLARSHIP FUNDS, MISCELLANEOUS FUNDS and STABILIZATION FUNDS, each with SUBTOTALS.
rows.notes: A RICHER SCHEDULE THAN FY2019'S -- this year the town added a market-value and unrealised-gain presentation the FY2019 report does not have, and the title changed from 'TRUST FUNDS STABILIZATION FUNDS' to 'TRUST AND OPEB FUNDS'. LIMITATION: the 188-character clip cuts the last one and a half columns, so ENDING MARKET VALUE is unrecoverable and CHANGE IN UNREALIZED GAIN/LOSS is cut mid-number. The first eight columns are complete. Stabilization detail: STABILIZATION $1,811,952.91 principal + $422,252.00 transferred in, ending cash $2,447,755.21; OPEB TRUST $350,000.00 + $110,000.00 in, ending $498,174.04 (against $210,231 at FY2019); SEWER CAPITAL RESERVE STAB $83,021.00 + $10,000.00 in; SEWER OPEB TRUST $1,312.00 + $656.00 in. The Dora Haven Cowdry Scholarship at $383,523.07 principal remains the largest single trust. Note 'OPES TRUST' and 'SEWER OPE TRUST' are OCR corruptions of OPEB.

rows.name: Five year outstanding debt as of 30 June 2021
rows.printed_heading: (title band and year headings lost; contents page calls it 'Five Year Outstanding Debt')
rows.what_it_is: Long-term and short-term indebtedness by purpose, inside and outside the general debt limit, for five fiscal years.
rows.columns: purpose | FY2021 | FY2020 | FY2019 | FY2018 | FY2017
rows.layout: Six columns, most-recent-first; the header row and the opening rows were lost with the top band.
rows.notes: OVERLAPS THE FY2019 REPORT'S EQUIVALENT BY THREE YEARS AND AGREES WITH IT EXACTLY -- FY2019, FY2018 and FY2017 totals are identical in both documents. That makes this the checkable version of the series. Schools remain the dominant component: 29,760,000 of 32,818,200 outside the general debt limit. The same footnote is printed: '(1) Principal amount only. Excludes lease and installment purchase obligations, overlapping debt and unfunded pension liability.'

rows.name: Authorized unissued debt and prospective financing
rows.printed_heading: Authorized Unissued Debt and Prospective Financing
rows.what_it_is: Debt voted but not yet borrowed, by purpose.
rows.layout: Two columns below the five-year debt table.
rows.notes: The purposes survive (School Feasibility Study Bond, School Construction, Land Acquisition, Sewer Construction twice, Pavement Management Plan, Artificial Turf Field & Track, Ladder Truck-Fire Department) but EVERY amount and the total are missing. Unusable for figures. The FY2019 report's version of the same table does carry four of the amounts.

rows.name: Debt repayment schedule as of 30 June 2021
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG DEBT REPAYMENT SCHEDULE AS OF JUNE 30, 2021
rows.what_it_is: Year-by-year principal, interest and MWPAT administrative fee for every outstanding issue, FY2022 onward, with grand totals per year.
rows.grain: one component (principal / interest / admin fee / total) of one debt issue, across fiscal years
rows.layout: A wide landscape matrix over four pages; p43-44 carry the earlier years with the grand-total block, p45-46 continue into the 2030s and 2040s.
rows.notes: A LARGE RECOVERY AND THE BIGGEST DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE TWO YEARS. Unlike FY2019's equivalent -- which prints its grand-total rows as labels with no values -- this one carries a complete grand-total block with figures, so the town's forward debt-service profile is quotable: total debt service falls from $4,516,558 in FY2022 to $3,483,223 in FY2024 and $2,547,440 in FY2026, which is the 'significant reduction in debt service as we pay off the Public Safety Building and Primary School loans in 2024' the Finance Committee describes on p64. Individual issue rows are still patchy in places and OCR renders '$' as 'S' and '5' inconsistently ('S52,640' for $59,640, '$S50,000'), so per-issue figures need checking against the PDF. Issues named: MUNICIPAL PURPOSE; MASS WATER POOL 9, 13, 14, 19; MS-HS CONSTRUCTION (GOB SCH OF 2014 and OF 2015); SCH/SEWER/MPL REFUNDING (GOB MPL OF 2016); MASS WATER POLLUTION ABT TRUST-SEWER; MUNICIPAL PURPOSE LOAN/SCH CONSTRUCTION (GOB MPL OF 2017); DPW-ROADS GENERAL OBLIGATION (GOB PML OF 2018); MEADOW WOODS SEWER and WATER GENERAL OBLIGATION; MUNICIPAL PURPOSE LOAN SCH/DPW (GOB MPL OF 2020). The MWPAT footnote is printed: 'PAYMENT AMOUNTS TO BE SUBSIDIZED BY EQUITY EARNINGS AND CONTRACT ASSISTANCE PAYMENTS'.

rows.name: FY2021 collection of taxes -- receivables summary
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG / FY2021 COLLECTION OF TAXES / RECEIVABLES SUMMARY / JUNE 30, 2021
rows.what_it_is: Every receivable the Collector carried, by type and levy year: real estate back to the levy of 2007, personal property, motor vehicle excise, supplemental taxes, tax liens, foreclosures, deferrals, water and sewer user charges, utility liens and betterments.
rows.grain: one receivable type at one levy year
rows.columns: FISCAL YEAR | FORWARD | COMMITTMENTS | ABATEMENTS | PAYMENTS | REFUNDS | TRANSFER | ADJUSTMENTS | (balance)
rows.layout: Nine columns over three pages, heading block repeated at the top of each.
rows.notes: Cleaner than the FY2019 equivalent -- the GRAND TOTAL row survives through six columns rather than five and a bit. The ADJUSTMENTS and balance columns are still lost to the 188-character clip. The dormant real estate levies of 2007-2016 carry the identical balances they carried in FY2019 ($3,890.09, $15.90, $137.74, $21.01, $21.88, $22.49, $23.39, $341.22, $3.92), which is how uncollectable old receivables sit on the books unchanged year after year.

rows.name: Cemetery interments, 2021
rows.printed_heading: (month names serve as the headings)
rows.what_it_is: Every burial in the town cemeteries during 2021 with name, age, cemetery and lot, war service where applicable, and an asterisk marking cremations.
rows.columns: name | age | cemetery (North / South / N/W East with lot number) | (war service, in parentheses)
rows.layout: Two side-by-side month-ordered lists, with the totals block at the foot of the right column.
rows.notes: FULLY RECOVERED INCLUDING ITS TOTALS BLOCK -- which the FY2019 equivalent is not. 9 full burials and 37 cremations, total 46; the cremation share is 80%, against FY2019's 30 cremations. War service annotated: (WWII), (Korea), (Peace Time). One entry is a 20-year-old and an 81-year-old buried in adjacent lots on the same month (Althea and Bernard Robarge, N/W East #55). As in FY2019, the Cemetery Commission publishes every name while the Town Clerk's vital records are name-suppressed -- except that FY2021 prints no vital records report at all.

rows.name: Cultural Council funding awards
rows.printed_heading: CULTURAL COUNCIL FUNDING AWARDS
rows.what_it_is: The grants the Lunenburg Cultural Council made, by recipient and project.
rows.layout: Two columns, sixteen rows.
rows.notes: NO AMOUNT COLUMN SURVIVES -- the table as rendered carries only recipient and project title, so the grants cannot be valued from this text. The Arts Lottery Fund line in the special revenue funds table (p36) gives the envelope: $11,926.80 forward, $7,022.52 received, $1,059.29 disbursed. Recipients include the Library (five awards under three staff names), St. Bernard's High School, Clear Path for Veterans New England, and the Winchendon Music Festival. FY2019 carries no equivalent table -- its Cultural Council filed 'No Report Submitted'.

rows.name: Green Communities grant projects, FY2021
rows.printed_heading: GREEN COMMUNITIES COMMITTEE
rows.what_it_is: The projects funded from the town's Green Community Grant award, listed with the one amount that is broken out.
rows.layout: Bulleted list inside the committee's report.
rows.notes: Only one project carries a figure ($10,000 toward hybrid cruisers for the Police Department); the rest are named without amounts (Building Operator Training for DPW staff, retro-commissioning of the Public Safety Building heating system, water heater and insulation at the Boys & Girls Club, hot water system for the Primary School, LED lighting retrofit for the Middle/High School). The stated 'over $57,000' sits against the Green Communities Grant row in the special revenue funds table (p35): $895.95 forward, $52,020.75 received, $39,609.13 spent, $13,307.57 carried. A grant paying for a police vehicle and a school hot water system is exactly the kind of funding that makes a general fund line look flat while the underlying spending is not.

rows.name: Library service statistics, FY2021
rows.printed_heading: Adult Service Notes / Children's Service Notes / Teen Services Notes

rows.what_it_is: Every person paid by the Town or the schools in calendar 2021 with their gross wages, alphabetical by surname.
rows.layout: Two surname/first-name/amount column groups side by side per page, seven pages.
rows.notes: A MAJOR RECOVERY, AND THE SHARPEST CONTRAST WITH FY2019. Here the amounts survive: over 400 wage figures across the seven pages, in proper rows beside their names, where the FY2019 equivalent retains only 40 of roughly 570. This is now the usable published payroll of the two years -- gross wages per named individual, which is the closest thing the town publishes to a staffing cost. Examples: BROCHU KAREN 108,671.76; BURLINGAME CASEY 99,605.26; BROC JONATHAN 94,729.68; BUNNELL JAMES 92,372.84; BASSETT KRISTINE 90,184.53. Two caveats before using it: a handful of figures carry OCR digit damage (a comma read as a full stop, '15,718,68'), and gross wages include overtime, details and stipends, so a figure here is not a salary and not a full employment cost.

rows.notes: Reads as a diff against FY2019's version: 'SELECT BOARD/TOWN MANAGER' replaces 'BOARD OF SELECTMEN/TOWN MANAGER'; 'PAYROLL & BENEFITS' and 'ASST.
